records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 unconditionally refreshes directly through Salesforce instead of refreshOAuthTokens, preventing shared credentials from refreshing through the configured parent application and rejecting connection initialization even when the supplied access token remains valid.
records.rationale: The finding is accurate. Looking at packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts lines 72-91, the code directly calls fetch to Salesforce's OAuth endpoint without using the refreshOAuthTokens wrapper that other integrations use (e.g., Google Calendar at line 86-92, Office365 at lines 246-261, Zoom at lines 79-95). The diff shows that refreshOAuthTokens is imported but only parseRefreshTokenResponse is used. This means when APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is true and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is configured, Salesforce will still refresh tokens directly instead of through the parent
